title: Sindhu, Satwik-Chirag, and a Squad That Wants More Than Bronze. India Names Its Asian Games Badminton Team.
excerpt: BAI confirms a 20-member squad for the Aichi-Nagoya Games in September, blending Olympic experience with a rising generation of young talent.
body:
The Badminton Association of India has named its squad for the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, and the lineup reads like a who's who of Indian badminton. PV Sindhu, the two-time Asian Games medalist and Olympic icon, will lead the women's contingent. Lakshya Sen, India's top-ranked men's singles player, will spearhead the men's challenge. And Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty — the golden pair from the 2022 Asian Games — will return to defend their men's doubles crown.

The Games are scheduled from September 19 to October 4, 2026. India's squad was finalised after evaluating recent results from national and international tournaments and BWF rankings as of May 26.

## The Core: Experience Meets Ambition

Sindhu, now 31, remains one of India's most bankable medal prospects in any multi-sport event. The former world champion and two-time Olympic medalist brings a decade of big-stage experience to a tournament India have historically underperformed in until the 2022 breakthrough in Hangzhou, where the team secured five bronze medals along with the landmark Satwik-Chirag gold.

Sen has established himself as India's premier men's singles player. The 24-year-old from Almora carries the confidence of a runner-up finish at the All England Championships this year and was instrumental in India's bronze-medal campaign at the Thomas Cup earlier this season. He will be joined by rising star Ayush Shetty, the 2025 US Open champion who earned a silver medal at the Badminton Asia Championships.

The men's team retains much of the core that won a historic silver at the 2022 Asiad — HS Prannoy and Kidambi Srikanth both return, adding depth and experience in singles. In doubles, Hariharan Amsakarunan and MR Arjun provide a capable second pair alongside the formidable Satwik-Chirag combination.

## New Generation Steps Up

What makes this squad particularly interesting is the injection of young talent. Unnati Hooda, a BWF World Junior Championships medalist, joins Sindhu in women's singles. Tanvi Sharma, a silver medalist at the World Junior Championships, has been rewarded for her rapid rise. Thailand Masters champion Devika Sihag further strengthens the women's singles depth.

In doubles, Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand Pullela continue to anchor India's women's challenge, while mixed doubles pair Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto add versatility to the setup.

## Full Squad

**Individual Championship:**
- **Men's Singles:** Lakshya Sen, Ayush Shetty
- **Women's Singles:** PV Sindhu, Unnati Hooda
- **Men's Doubles:** Satwiksairaj Rankireddy / Chirag Shetty; Hariharan Amsakarunan / MR Arjun
- **Women's Doubles:** Treesa Jolly / Gayatri Gopichand; Kavipriya Selvam / Simran Singhi
- **Mixed Doubles:** Dhruv Kapila / Tanisha Crasto

**Team Championship:**
- **Men:** Sen, Shetty, Prannoy, Srikanth, Mannepalli, Satwik, Chirag, Hariharan, Arjun, Kapila
- **Women:** Sindhu, Hooda, Sihag, Sharma, Baruah, Jolly, Gopichand, Selvam, Singhi, Crasto

## Why NRIs Should Pay Attention

The Asian Games are the largest multi-sport event on the continent and a genuine barometer of India's sporting depth beyond cricket. For the diaspora, several storylines converge in Aichi-Nagoya. Sindhu, who was born in Hyderabad and has become a global ambassador for Indian sport, will be competing in what could be her final Asian Games. The Satwik-Chirag pair, whose gold in Hangzhou was celebrated across Indian communities worldwide, will attempt to become the first Indian badminton pair to defend an Asiad title.

India's 2022 haul of one gold and five bronzes was their best-ever performance at the Asian Games in badminton. A strong showing in Japan would further cement India's status as a genuine multi-discipline badminton power — and give the growing NRI community another reason to tune in beyond cricket.

*Sources: BAI, IANS, BWF, Revsportz*
